newsitem.title: USA: Maine officials urge $11 mln bond issue approval.
newsitem.headline: Maine officials urge $11 mln bond issue approval.

text.p: Maine officials are urging voters to approve $11 million of bonds for economic development, but the plan is opposed by Mary Adams, who also is leading an effort to defeat the clear-cutting referendums.

Adams, a former Assemblywoman and unsuccessful candidate for governor, said that Maine has borrowed enough money over the last few years and if companies need money, they should borrow it from banks, not the taxpayers.
If the plan is approved by the voters, $6 million would go to fund an agricultural loan and the remaining $5 million would be used to provide money for high-risk small businesses.
